direction: Explore new priority rules for the CVRP greedy construction by changing one score term at a time.

operations.target: one term of the priority score
operations.mechanism: Replace exactly one of the three terms (distance to the current node, distance to the depot, remaining capacity) with a different functional form and leave the other two unchanged, so the effect of the change is readable in the next round's numbers.
After the primary score, order the candidates whose primary scores are closest together by a secondary criterion; the stage has to stay cheap enough to fit the solver budget.
Keep the capacity filter, the construction order and the sign convention of the objective unchanged.

preserve: The problem interface, the evaluator and the search policy.
hypothesis: Replacing one score term per round and adding a cheap second ordering stage yields better routes than rewriting the whole score at once.

research_activity.question: Are the priority scores this search writes invariant to the numerical scale at which the same instance is expressed?
research_activity.finding_summary: Measured on the dev suite. The near-tie gate written in the previous batch is not invariant to coordinate scale: re-expressing the same instances at 1e-2 and 1e-3 of nominal size raises the share of steps entering the gate from 1.3% to 64% and 83%, and degrades the scale-normalised objective from 10.92 to 16.20 and 33.52 (+48%, +207%). At nominal scale the gate fires on only 1.3% of steps, so it is nearly dead where the suite lives: too wide when the instance shrinks, too narrow at nominal. The width adds an absolute length to a span-proportional term. Keeping only the span-proportional part removes the scale dependence (spread 0.39% over four scales) but gives back 1.92% at nominal, so invariance is not a win on its own: the nominal regression has to stay near zero too.
